transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi... yeah, thank you. Well, I came in because, um, I've been trying to turn my art into a real freelance business lately. I mostly do watercolors, like botanical prints and stuff. My aunt actually used to grow these huge hydrangeas, and I spent all last summer trying to get the exact shade of blue right on paper. It's surprisingly hard because the soil acidity actually changes the flower's color in real life, you know? Like if you put coffee grounds in the dirt it turns them blue... wait, sorry, what was I saying? 

Right, the business. Anyway, ever since I tried to make it an actual business, I just keep getting so wound up over the invoices and client messages. I had this one lady who wanted a portrait of her iguana and she emailed me like four times a day... but yeah, I get so stressed that I just avoid the messages completely. And then it piles up until I'm just sitting there crying at my kitchen table, or I end up forgetting to do normal stuff, like paying my own electric bill.
Do you find yourself thinking about the invoices, client messages, or art repeatedly, even when you're trying to focus on something else?

Um, no, not really. If I'm doing something else, I'm usually pretty focused on that. Like yesterday, I was watching this documentary about competitive dog grooming to just take my mind off things. Have you ever seen those? They dye these poodles to look like tigers or, like, pandas. It's actually kind of fascinating from an artistic standpoint, the way they sculpt the fur. I can barely get my own hair to hold a curl, let alone shear a dog into a perfect square. 

My cousin had a toy poodle once named Barnaby, and he was honestly the meanest little dog. He actually bit the mailman twice. The post office stopped delivering to her house, so she had to get a P.O. box... which is such a hassle because the post office downtown never has any parking, and the meter maids there are just ruthless. I got a ticket there once when I was just dropping off a letter. 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, thinking about the invoices. No, I don't really have them playing on a loop in my head or anything. I just try not to think about them at all.
Do you feel an overwhelming urge to perform specific rituals or behaviors?

Um, no, not really. I don't have any rituals or anything like that. I do have a really specific way I organize my paints, though, but that's just because if you mix up the cool reds and the warm reds, everything gets muddy. I learned that the hard way when I was taking this color theory class at the community college. The professor was this older guy who always wore these really loud, patterned bow ties. Like, every single day, a different bow tie. I think one had little rubber ducks on it. 

Actually, speaking of ducks, there's this pond near my apartment, and people are always feeding them bread, which you're really not supposed to do. It's so bad for them. You're supposed to give them frozen peas or oats. I bought a bag of frozen peas once just to feed them, but then my freezer broke and everything melted. It was such a disaster. My landlord took three days to send someone out to fix it, and I had to throw away all my ice cream. I had this really good pistachio gelato in there, too. Have you ever tried pistachio gelato? It's way better than regular pistachio ice cream, it's so much creamier. 

But, um... wait, rituals. Right. No, I don't have any urges to do things over and over like that. Just the paint organizing, but that's just practical.
Do you often find yourself avoiding things that remind you of your freelance business or the stress it causes?

Um, yeah, actually. I do avoid it. Like, if I see an email notification pop up on my phone, I'll just swipe it away immediately and put my phone in another room. I bought this really nice ceramic bowl at a craft fair last month, and I've started just dropping my phone in there when I can't deal with it. The bowl has this gorgeous glaze on it, kind of a seafoam green with these little flecks of gold. The artist said she fired it in a raku kiln, which is this whole intense process where they pull the pottery out while it's still glowing red hot and put it in a metal trash can full of combustible stuff, like sawdust or newspaper. 

My uncle actually tried to build a kiln in his backyard once. He's always getting into these weird hobbies. One year it was beekeeping, and the next it was making his own artisanal cheeses. The cheese phase was honestly the worst because his whole house smelled like old socks for six months. He tried to give us this wheel of gouda for Christmas, and my mom just smiled and nodded, but I know she threw it straight in the garbage the second we got home. She's so polite like that, she can't stand to hurt anyone's feelings. I think I get that from her, which is probably why I hate telling clients no when they ask for ridiculous revisions on their paintings. 

Like that iguana lady, she wanted me to add a tiny top hat to the iguana after I had already finished the watercolor. You can't just paint over watercolor! It's transparent! But um... what was the question? Oh, right, avoiding things. Yeah, I definitely just avoid looking at the emails or my invoice spreadsheet. I haven't opened my laptop in three days because I know the tabs are just sitting there waiting for me.
Do you feel anxious when interacting with clients or potential clients for your freelance business?

Um, anxious? I don't know if I'd say anxious, exactly. It's more like... I just don't really want to deal with them. Like, I just want to paint, you know? But then you have to talk to them, and they always want to chat about their pets or their kids before they even tell you what they want. Which is fine, I guess, but I had this one client last year who spent forty-five minutes telling me about her son's travel soccer team. Do you know how much those travel teams cost? It's insane. They fly these ten-year-olds to Florida for tournaments. When I was ten, my parents wouldn't even buy me the name-brand Lunchables. I always got the generic ones where the cheese tasted like plastic. 

Actually, I still kind of love those generic cheese squares. I bought a pack last week when I was at the grocery store. I go to this one specific grocery store across town because they have this amazing bakery section. They make these sourdough boules that are just... incredible. The crust is perfectly crunchy, and the inside is so chewy. I tried to make sourdough during the pandemic, like everyone else, but my starter died after two weeks. I named him Dough-Joe, like a dojo, you know? Because he was supposed to be strong. But he just got really liquidy and smelled like nail polish remover. I read online that means it's hungry, but no matter how much flour I fed it, it just wouldn't bubble. 

I ended up pouring it down the garbage disposal, which was a huge mistake because it basically turned into cement in the pipes. The plumber who came to fix it was so nice, though. He showed me how to reset the disposal with this little red button on the bottom. I had no idea that was even there! It's saved me like three times since then. 

But um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, interacting with clients. Yeah, I don't know about anxious. I just... I don't really like doing it, so I kind of just avoid it when I can.
Has avoiding invoices, client messages, or other business-related tasks interfered with your daily life or relationships in any significant way?

Um, yeah, I guess it kind of has. It's definitely affecting my freelance stuff. Like, I keep putting off replying to clients, and then I get so wrapped up in trying to organize my art display for this upcoming local fair that I totally forget about other things. I actually missed paying my electric bill last month because of it. I had the envelope sitting right on my kitchen counter, next to this really cool vintage toaster I found at a thrift store. 

Have you ever been to the thrift store on 4th Street? They have the most amazing mid-century kitchen appliances. The toaster I got is this shiny chrome one from the 1950s, and it still works perfectly! It makes the toast so much crispier than those cheap plastic ones you buy nowadays. I tried to make avocado toast with it the other day, but the avocados I bought were completely brown inside. It’s so frustrating when you buy avocados and they feel perfectly ripe at the store, but then you cut them open and it’s just mush. I ended up having to throw them in my compost bin. 

I started composting a few months ago because I read it’s really good for your garden. I’m trying to grow some heirloom tomatoes on my balcony, but the squirrels keep digging up the dirt. They are so bold! One of them actually sat on my railing and just stared at me while I was drinking my coffee yesterday. I tried to shoo it away, but it just flicked its tail at me. I think it lives in the big oak tree behind my building. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the business stuff interfering. Yeah, so missing that utility payment was pretty bad, and I know I need to get back to my clients, but I just keep getting distracted by the art display and... everything else.
Do you feel overwhelmed by guilt or worry when you avoid dealing with your freelance business tasks?

Um, yeah, the worry is... it's a lot, honestly. That's actually why I came in to see you, because ever since I tried to turn my art into a real freelance business, I just keep getting so wound up over the invoices and all those client messages. And then I avoid them until I'm literally just sitting there crying at my kitchen table, or forgetting normal stuff like paying a bill. 

My kitchen table is actually where I do most of my painting, too. It’s this gorgeous reclaimed wood farmhouse table I found on Facebook Marketplace. The guy who sold it to me was moving to Colorado to start an alpaca farm. Can you imagine? Alpacas are so funny-looking. They have those really big eyes and fluffy necks. I saw a video once of an alpaca getting sheared and it looked so ridiculously skinny underneath all that fluff. I think they use the fleece to make yarn, which makes sense because I knitted this scarf once out of alpaca yarn and it was the softest thing I've ever touched. I tried to knit a matching beanie for it, but I dropped a stitch somewhere in the middle and it ended up looking like a lopsided bowl. I ended up giving it to my neighbor's toddler to use as a sleeping bag for his stuffed animals. He has this massive collection of stuffed dinosaurs. The T-Rex is his favorite, but he can't pronounce it right, so he calls it a 'Tea-Rocks.' It's so cute. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Something about feeling guilty?
Have you noticed any problems in your relationships with friends or family because of your avoidance of business tasks?

Um, with friends and family? Not really, no. They don't really know much about the business side of things. My mom just thinks it's nice that I'm painting again. She always loved my paintings when I was little. She used to frame them and put them up all over the house, even the really bad ones where the people looked like stick figures with giant heads. 

Actually, I found one of those old paintings when I was helping her clean out her attic last weekend. The attic was so dusty, I was sneezing the whole time. I think I'm allergic to dust mites or something. I bought this special air purifier for my apartment because of it, and it has this little light that changes color depending on how clean the air is. It’s usually blue, but whenever I cook, it turns bright red. I’m not sure if that means I’m a bad cook or if my stove is just really smoky. I made stir-fry the other night and the smoke alarm went off, which was terrifying because my cat, Barnaby, completely freaked out and hid under the sofa for three hours. I had to lure him out with tuna water. He loves tuna water, but only from the cans that are packed in spring water, not the ones in oil. If I give him the oil kind, he just sniffs it and gives me this look of absolute betrayal. 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my family. Yeah, no, the business stuff hasn't really caused any problems with them. I just keep that part to myself.
Do you think you avoid interacting with clients because you're afraid of what they might think of you or your work?

Um, no, I don't think it's that. I mean, I know my art is good, and people usually really like it when they see it. It's just the... the business part of it that freaks me out. The invoices and the formal emails. But the art itself, I'm really proud of. Like, I just finished this watercolor of a blue heron last week. I actually had to go to the art supply store downtown just to get a specific shade of cerulean blue for the water. 

I love that store so much, it always smells like cedar and linseed oil. But the parking there is just an absolute nightmare. I had to park three blocks away and right as I got out of my car, it started pouring rain. I didn't have an umbrella, so I had to use this empty canvas tote bag over my head to keep my hair dry. It was one of those canvas bags they give out for free at the farmer's market. I try to go to the farmer's market every Sunday to get these fresh sourdough loaves from this guy named Ted. Ted has this massive beard, like, it goes all the way down to his chest, and he told me he puts this special oil in it that smells like pine needles. 

I actually bought some pine-scented candles once because I thought it would make my apartment feel cozy, like a cabin in the woods, but they just made the whole place smell like a cheap car air freshener. You know those little cardboard green trees people hang from their rearview mirrors? My dad always had one of those in his truck when I was growing up. He drove this beat-up old Chevy that made a horrible rattling noise whenever he went over forty miles an hour. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Something about my clients not liking my work? Yeah, no, they like it fine. It's just... actually doing the business part and sending the emails that I can't seem to do.
Do you think you avoid dealing with invoices and client messages because you're worried about being judged or criticized?

Um, judged? No, I don't think so. I mean, my clients are usually really nice. It's not that I think they're going to yell at me or say I'm doing a bad job. It's just... I don't know, it's just the actual act of doing it that feels like too much. Looking at the numbers and figuring out the taxes and all that. Taxes are so confusing. I tried to use one of those online tax programs last year, and it kept asking me all these questions about deductions and depreciation, and I had no idea what any of it meant. 

I ended up calling my uncle Dave for help because he used to be an accountant, but he talks so slow. Like, painfully slow. And he always breathes really heavily into the phone, like he just ran up a flight of stairs. He lives in Florida now, in one of those retirement communities where everyone drives golf carts everywhere. He sent me a picture of his golf cart last Christmas, and he had put these little reindeer antlers on the roof and a red nose on the front bumper. It was kind of funny, but also a little weird. He said they have a golf cart parade every year, and last year someone decorated theirs like a giant flamingo. Flamingos are such strange birds. Why do they stand on one leg? I read once that it's to conserve body heat, but they live in warm places, so that doesn't really make sense, does it? 

But um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, about being criticized? Yeah, no, it's not that. It's just the business stuff itself that I can't handle.
Do you think you avoid dealing with invoices and client messages because you're afraid of failing at your freelance business?

Um, afraid of failing? I don't... I don't know if it's fear of failing, exactly. I mean, I know I'm a good artist. People buy my stuff. It's just... the thought of opening those emails and seeing all the requests and the deadlines, it just makes my chest feel all tight. Like when I try to drink coffee too fast in the morning. I've been trying to switch to tea, actually, because coffee makes me jittery. I got this loose-leaf chamomile blend from this little shop down the street. The woman who owns it is so nice, she always gives me free samples. Last time, she gave me this peppermint one that she said was good for digestion. 

I don't really have digestion problems, but I drank it anyway. It tasted kind of like toothpaste, to be honest. I used to use this organic toothpaste that tasted like fennel, which was awful. It was like brushing my teeth with black licorice. I hate black licorice. My grandma used to keep a bowl of it on her coffee table, the kind that looks like little black jellybeans. We'd always try to sneak the red ones when she wasn't looking, but she always knew. She had eyes in the back of her head, I swear. She could tell if we even touched the bowl. 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Failing? Yeah, I don't think it's about failing. It's just... the business side is just so overwhelming, I can't even bring myself to look at it.
Do you think you would feel relieved if you weren't doing the freelance business anymore?

Um, relieved? I'm not sure... I haven't really thought about just stopping completely. I mean, if I wasn't doing my art, what would I even do? Just get a regular job again? I used to work at this bakery a few years ago, and I don't really want to go back to that. I always came home covered in flour. Like, a ridiculous amount of flour. It would get all in my hair and my shoes, and even all over my car seats. 

My car seats are black, so you could see every single white speck. I tried vacuuming it with one of those little hand-held vacuums, but it barely had any suction. I bought it off an infomercial late at night when I couldn't sleep. You know those commercials that come on at like 2 AM? The guy was yelling about how it could pick up bowling balls. Which is so stupid, why would anyone need to vacuum up a bowling ball? I don't even like bowling anyway. The shoes they make you wear are just so gross. You just know a thousand other people have sweat in them. My cousin rented a pair once and got a terrible case of athlete's foot, and he had to use this special cream that smelled exactly like sulfur. It made his whole house smell like rotten eggs for a week. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? If I'd feel relieved if I quit? Yeah, I don't know. I'm really not sure. I haven't really pictured not doing it.
Do you feel like your avoidance of business tasks is affecting your overall well-being or daily life in a significant way?

Um, yeah, I guess it is affecting things. Like, I keep putting off client replies, which I know is bad for my freelance work, and I even missed a utility payment the other day because I was just avoiding looking at any of my bills. I was trying so hard to just focus on getting my art display ready for this weekend, but everything else is just slipping. 

Speaking of the art display, I had to buy these new hanging wires for it because the old ones got all tangled up in this box in my closet. I don't even know how they got so tangled, it's like they tied themselves in knots while I wasn't looking. Kind of like earphones used to do before everything went wireless. I finally got a pair of those wireless earbuds, but they fall out of my ears if I chew too aggressively. I was eating an apple the other day—a Honeycrisp, they're definitely the best kind of apple, way better than Red Delicious, which aren't even delicious at all, they just taste like wet sand. Anyway, I bit into it and my left earbud just popped right out and rolled under the refrigerator. 

I had to use a broom handle to fish it out, and you wouldn't believe the amount of dust bunnies under there. I really need to sweep more often. My cat, Barnaby, loves chasing the dust bunnies, which is cute but also kind of gross when he tries to eat them. He’s an orange tabby, and they always say orange cats share one brain cell, which is honestly so true for him. He spent ten minutes yesterday fighting his own reflection in the oven door. 

But um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, if it's affecting my daily life? Yeah, it really is. Missing that utility payment was pretty stressful, and the client stuff is just piling up.
Do you think your avoidance of business tasks is because you're afraid that if you face them, you might find out you're not as good at running a business as you thought?

Um, afraid of finding out I'm not good at running a business? I... I don't really know. I haven't thought about it like that. I guess I just know I'm good at the art part, but the business part is just... a lot. Like, doing taxes and tracking expenses. I bought this special notebook to track my expenses, it has these really nice thick pages. I love good stationery. 

There's this store downtown that sells all these imported Japanese pens and notebooks, and I could spend hours in there. The pens write so smoothly, they don't smudge at all. I hate when pens smudge, especially since I'm left-handed. Everything I write just ends up smeared all over the side of my hand. When I was in school, my teachers used to get so annoyed because my papers were always covered in gray smudges. One teacher actually told me to just write with my right hand instead, which is crazy, right? You can't just switch hands like that. I tried it once and it looked like a chicken scratched on the paper. 

My aunt actually has chickens, she lives out in the country. She gets fresh eggs every morning. They have these really bright orange yolks, not like the pale yellow ones you get at the grocery store. She gave me a carton last week, and I tried making a soufflé, but it completely collapsed. I guess I opened the oven door too soon. It was so disappointing. 

But um... what were you saying? Oh, about not being good at the business stuff? I don't know, maybe. I just really don't like thinking about it.
Do you think you would be able to handle your freelance business tasks if you had help or support from someone else?

Um, if I had help? I don't know... maybe? I haven't really thought about asking anyone for help. I mean, my sister offered to look at my spreadsheet once, but she's an accountant and she gets really intense about numbers. Like, she has this whole color-coded system for everything in her life. Even her spice rack is alphabetized. 

I went over to her house for dinner last month and she made this curry, but she used way too much turmeric because she said it was good for inflammation. It stained my favorite white sweater. I tried soaking it in club soda, then I tried this stain remover pen, but it just left a weird yellow ring. I read online that you can use lemon juice and leave it in the sun, but it's been so cloudy lately. The weather here is just so unpredictable. Last Tuesday it was almost seventy degrees, and then by Thursday we had frost on the windshields. I had to use an old credit card to scrape my window because I couldn't find my ice scraper. It was a card from this department store that went out of business years ago. 

They used to have the best perfume counter. They would give you those little glass sample vials instead of just spraying it on a piece of cardboard. I had this one sample that smelled exactly like lilacs, and I kept it in my purse for months until the little plastic stopper broke and it leaked everywhere. My purse smelled like a flower shop for a year. 

Wait, sorry, what did you ask me? About having someone help me with the business stuff? I guess... maybe it would help. I'm just not sure who I would even ask, besides my sister.
Do you think you would feel less overwhelmed by your business tasks if you knew you couldn't fail at them?

Um, if I couldn't fail? I... I don't really know. I've never really thought about it like that, because, well, you can always fail, right? Like, even when you think you have everything perfectly planned out. I tried to plan out this whole vegetable garden in my backyard last spring. I drew out this little grid on graph paper and everything. 

I planted tomatoes, zucchini, and these little bell peppers. But then the rabbits got into it. They just ate everything right down to the little green nubs. I even put up this chicken wire fence, but they dug right under it. My neighbor, Mr. Henderson, told me I should plant marigolds around the edge because rabbits hate the smell, but I'm pretty sure his cat is the one actually keeping the rabbits out of his yard. His cat is this huge, fluffy Maine Coon named Barnaby—wait, no, my cat is Barnaby. His cat is named Bartholomew. It's so confusing because they both start with B. 

Bartholomew always sits on my fence and just stares at me while I'm trying to read on the patio. It's kind of unnerving, honestly. Like he knows all my secrets. I was reading this mystery novel out there the other day, and it was so good, but the ending was completely ruined because someone had torn out the last three pages. I got it from the used bookstore downtown, the one that smells like old paper and coffee. They have a little café inside, but their espresso machine is always broken. 

But um... sorry, I lost track. What were you saying? Oh, about not failing at the business stuff? I mean, I guess if I knew for sure I couldn't mess it up, it might be less scary. But I don't really know how that would even work.
Do you think your avoidance of business tasks is mostly because you are afraid of failing at them?

Um, afraid of failing? I... I don't know, maybe? I guess I just feel like I don't know what I'm doing when it comes to that stuff, so it's easier to just... not do it. But failing is just such a strong word, you know? It reminds me of getting a failing grade in school. 

I actually failed a pottery class once in community college. Well, I didn't fail it, I got a D, but it felt like failing. The instructor said my pieces lacked structural integrity. I was trying to make this really tall vase, but the clay was too wet and it just kind of slumped over on the wheel. It looked like a melted candle. I tried to save it by turning it into a bowl, but the sides were too thin and it cracked in the kiln. 

The kiln room was always so hot, especially in the summer. They had this one little fan in the corner that just blew hot air around. I used to go get a slushie from the gas station across the street just to cool down. They had this blue raspberry flavor that would turn your whole mouth blue. I went to a job interview once right after drinking one, and I didn't realize until I got home and looked in the mirror that my teeth were completely blue. I didn't get the job, obviously. It was for a receptionist position at a dentist's office, which makes it even worse. 

Wait, what were we talking about? Oh, failing the business tasks. I don't know. I just... I don't like dealing with it. It's just a lot.
Is your avoidance of business tasks mostly because you're afraid of failing at them or is there another reason?

Um, another reason besides failing? I'm not really sure. I mean, maybe? It's just... it's all just sitting there, waiting for me to do it, and I just look at the pile of receipts and the emails and I just feel this... weight, I guess? 

Like, speaking of weight, I tried to get back into lifting weights last week. I bought these little five-pound dumbbells from a garage sale. The lady selling them had the most amazing collection of vintage teacups. She said she spent thirty years collecting them from estate sales all over the state. She had this one that was painted with these tiny, perfect little hummingbirds, and the saucer had a gold rim. I almost bought it, but I don't even drink tea. Coffee is my thing. 

I have this French press that I use every morning, but the plunger part is getting kind of wobbly. I tried to tighten the little screw at the bottom, but I dropped it down the sink drain. I had to take the whole U-pipe thing apart under the sink to get it out. It was so gross down there. There was this weird black sludge that smelled like old onions, even though I haven't cooked with onions in weeks because they always make my eyes water so badly. I tried that trick where you chew gum while you chop them, but it didn't work at all. I just ended up crying into my cutting board while chewing peppermint gum. 

Wait... sorry, I did it again, didn't I? You were asking about the business stuff and if there's another reason I avoid it. I don't know, honestly. I don't really have a specific reason other than it just feels like too much, and I don't want to look at it.
Is there something specific about the business tasks themselves that makes you want to avoid them, beyond just the fear of failing at them?

Um, something specific about the tasks? I... I don't really think so. It's just... I don't know, it's all just numbers and forms and things I don't understand. Like taxes. Taxes are so confusing. My uncle used to do my taxes for me, but he moved to Florida last year. He bought this little condo near the beach, but he says the seagulls are a menace. They stole a whole hot dog right out of his hand while he was walking on the boardwalk. 

He was so mad about it, but honestly, I think seagulls are kind of smart. Like, they know exactly when to swoop in. I watched this documentary once about crows and how they can remember human faces. If you're mean to a crow, it will tell all its crow friends, and they'll all hold a grudge against you. That's why I always try to leave out unsalted peanuts on my porch railing. But the squirrels usually get to them first. 

There's this one squirrel with a little notch in his ear—I call him Vincent, like Vincent van Gogh. He's so bold, he'll come right up to the glass door and stare at me while I'm eating breakfast. I usually eat oatmeal, but I ran out of brown sugar the other day, so I tried putting maple syrup in it instead. It was okay, but it made it kind of runny. I buy the real maple syrup, the kind in the glass bottle shaped like a leaf. It's expensive, but it's so much better than the fake stuff. 

Oh, wait. Sorry. You asked if there was something specific about the tasks. No, not really. I just... I don't know. I just really don't want to do them.
Is your avoidance of business tasks mostly because you're afraid of failing at them or is there another reason that's causing you to avoid them?

Um, another reason... I don't... I don't think so. I really don't know why I keep doing this, avoiding it all. It just feels like this big, heavy cloud hanging over me. 

Speaking of clouds, it looked like it was going to rain all morning, didn't it? The sky was that weird, bruised purple color. I actually love when it rains, as long as I don't have to drive in it. My car's windshield wipers are making this awful screeching sound. I tried to replace them myself last month, but I bought the wrong size at the auto parts store. The guy working there was trying to be helpful, but he kept calling me "sweetheart," which I really hate. My grandfather used to call me sweetheart, but he always had a butterscotch candy in his pocket for me, so it was different. 

He had this old leather armchair that smelled like pipe tobacco and peppermint. I inherited it when he passed away, but my cat completely ruined the armrests. She just uses it as a giant scratching post, no matter how many actual scratching posts I buy her. I bought this huge, elaborate cat tree online, and it came in like a hundred pieces. The instructions were just pictures, no words, and I put the whole middle section on backward. Now it leans to the left, but she sleeps in the little hammock part anyway. 

Wait, sorry. I'm doing it again. You're asking about the business stuff and if there's another reason. I just... I don't have a good answer for you. I just really, really don't want to do it, and I don't know why.

doctor.question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

target_item.name: Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response
target_item.manifestation: I came in because ever since I tried to turn my art into a real freelance business, I keep getting wound up over invoices and client messages, then I avoid them until I'm crying at my kitchen table or forgetting normal stuff like paying a bill.
target_item.reason: This is the first reply of the consultation, so I must return the chief complaint symptom code (S081).

patient.answer:
Hi... yeah, thank you. Well, I came in because, um, I've been trying to turn my art into a real freelance business lately. I mostly do watercolors, like botanical prints and stuff. My aunt actually used to grow these huge hydrangeas, and I spent all last summer trying to get the exact shade of blue right on paper. It's surprisingly hard because the soil acidity actually changes the flower's color in real life, you know? Like if you put coffee grounds in the dirt it turns them blue... wait, sorry, what was I saying? 

Right, the business. Anyway, ever since I tried to make it an actual business, I just keep getting so wound up over the invoices and client messages. I had this one lady who wanted a portrait of her iguana and she emailed me like four times a day... but yeah, I get so stressed that I just avoid the messages completely. And then it piles up until I'm just sitting there crying at my kitchen table, or I end up forgetting to do normal stuff, like paying my own electric bill.

inference.note: Added potential anxiety and stress-related disorders due to patient's reported stress and avoidance behaviors

doctor.question: Do you find yourself thinking about the invoices, client messages, or art repeatedly, even when you're trying to focus on something else?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about intrusive, repetitive thoughts regarding the stressors (invoices, messages, art), which sounds like checking for symptoms of PTSD, OCD, or GAD (like rumination or intrusive thoughts). My profile mentions getting wound up, avoiding messages, crying, and forgetting things, but does not specifically mention having repetitive/intrusive thoughts about them when trying to focus elsewhere.

patient.answer:
Um, no, not really. If I'm doing something else, I'm usually pretty focused on that. Like yesterday, I was watching this documentary about competitive dog grooming to just take my mind off things. Have you ever seen those? They dye these poodles to look like tigers or, like, pandas. It's actually kind of fascinating from an artistic standpoint, the way they sculpt the fur. I can barely get my own hair to hold a curl, let alone shear a dog into a perfect square. 

My cousin had a toy poodle once named Barnaby, and he was honestly the meanest little dog. He actually bit the mailman twice. The post office stopped delivering to her house, so she had to get a P.O. box... which is such a hassle because the post office downtown never has any parking, and the meter maids there are just ruthless. I got a ticket there once when I was just dropping off a letter. 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, right, thinking about the invoices. No, I don't really have them playing on a loop in my head or anything. I just try not to think about them at all.

doctor.intent: determine presence of compulsions
doctor.question: Do you feel an overwhelming urge to perform specific rituals or behaviors?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about compulsions or rituals (symptoms of OCD), which are not part of my symptom profile for Adjustment Disorder.

patient.answer:
Um, no, not really. I don't have any rituals or anything like that. I do have a really specific way I organize my paints, though, but that's just because if you mix up the cool reds and the warm reds, everything gets muddy. I learned that the hard way when I was taking this color theory class at the community college. The professor was this older guy who always wore these really loud, patterned bow ties. Like, every single day, a different bow tie. I think one had little rubber ducks on it. 

Actually, speaking of ducks, there's this pond near my apartment, and people are always feeding them bread, which you're really not supposed to do. It's so bad for them. You're supposed to give them frozen peas or oats. I bought a bag of frozen peas once just to feed them, but then my freezer broke and everything melted. It was such a disaster. My landlord took three days to send someone out to fix it, and I had to throw away all my ice cream. I had this really good pistachio gelato in there, too. Have you ever tried pistachio gelato? It's way better than regular pistachio ice cream, it's so much creamier. 

But, um... wait, rituals. Right. No, I don't have any urges to do things over and over like that. Just the paint organizing, but that's just practical.

doctor.intent: determine presence of avoidance behavior
doctor.question: Do you often find yourself avoiding things that remind you of your freelance business or the stress it causes?

target_item.reason: The doctor is asking about avoidance symptoms related to the freelance business stress. While my chief complaint mentions avoiding messages, the specific symptom profile items do not have an explicit key for 'avoidance of reminders'. The 'Stress_Related_Maladaptive_Response' was already used for the chief complaint. There is no specific key for avoidance behavior in the provided profile.

patient.answer:
Um, yeah, actually. I do avoid it. Like, if I see an email notification pop up on my phone, I'll just swipe it away immediately and put my phone in another room. I bought this really nice ceramic bowl at a craft fair last month, and I've started just dropping my phone in there when I can't deal with it. The bowl has this gorgeous glaze on it, kind of a seafoam green with these little flecks of gold. The artist said she fired it in a raku kiln, which is this whole intense process where they pull the pottery out while it's still glowing red hot and put it in a metal trash can full of combustible stuff, like sawdust or newspaper. 

My uncle actually tried to build a kiln in his backyard once. He's always getting into these weird hobbies. One year it was beekeeping, and the next it was making his own artisanal cheeses. The cheese phase was honestly the worst because his whole house smelled like old socks for six months. He tried to give us this wheel of gouda for Christmas, and my mom just smiled and nodded, but I know she threw it straight in the garbage the second we got home. She's so polite like that, she can't stand to hurt anyone's feelings. I think I get that from her, which is probably why I hate telling clients no when they ask for ridiculous revisions on their paintings. 

Like that iguana lady, she wanted me to add a tiny top hat to the iguana after I had already finished the watercolor. You can't just paint over watercolor! It's transparent! But um... what was the question? Oh, right, avoiding things. Yeah, I definitely just avoid looking at the emails or my invoice spreadsheet. I haven't opened my laptop in three days because I know the tabs are just sitting there waiting for me.

patient.answer:
Um, anxious? I don't know if I'd say anxious, exactly. It's more like... I just don't really want to deal with them. Like, I just want to paint, you know? But then you have to talk to them, and they always want to chat about their pets or their kids before they even tell you what they want. Which is fine, I guess, but I had this one client last year who spent forty-five minutes telling me about her son's travel soccer team. Do you know how much those travel teams cost? It's insane. They fly these ten-year-olds to Florida for tournaments. When I was ten, my parents wouldn't even buy me the name-brand Lunchables. I always got the generic ones where the cheese tasted like plastic. 

Actually, I still kind of love those generic cheese squares. I bought a pack last week when I was at the grocery store. I go to this one specific grocery store across town because they have this amazing bakery section. They make these sourdough boules that are just... incredible. The crust is perfectly crunchy, and the inside is so chewy. I tried to make sourdough during the pandemic, like everyone else, but my starter died after two weeks. I named him Dough-Joe, like a dojo, you know? Because he was supposed to be strong. But he just got really liquidy and smelled like nail polish remover. I read online that means it's hungry, but no matter how much flour I fed it, it just wouldn't bubble. 

I ended up pouring it down the garbage disposal, which was a huge mistake because it basically turned into cement in the pipes. The plumber who came to fix it was so nice, though. He showed me how to reset the disposal with this little red button on the bottom. I had no idea that was even there! It's saved me like three times since then. 

But um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, interacting with clients. Yeah, I don't know about anxious. I just... I don't really like doing it, so I kind of just avoid it when I can.

patient.answer:
Um, yeah, I guess it kind of has. It's definitely affecting my freelance stuff. Like, I keep putting off replying to clients, and then I get so wrapped up in trying to organize my art display for this upcoming local fair that I totally forget about other things. I actually missed paying my electric bill last month because of it. I had the envelope sitting right on my kitchen counter, next to this really cool vintage toaster I found at a thrift store. 

Have you ever been to the thrift store on 4th Street? They have the most amazing mid-century kitchen appliances. The toaster I got is this shiny chrome one from the 1950s, and it still works perfectly! It makes the toast so much crispier than those cheap plastic ones you buy nowadays. I tried to make avocado toast with it the other day, but the avocados I bought were completely brown inside. It’s so frustrating when you buy avocados and they feel perfectly ripe at the store, but then you cut them open and it’s just mush. I ended up having to throw them in my compost bin. 

I started composting a few months ago because I read it’s really good for your garden. I’m trying to grow some heirloom tomatoes on my balcony, but the squirrels keep digging up the dirt. They are so bold! One of them actually sat on my railing and just stared at me while I was drinking my coffee yesterday. I tried to shoo it away, but it just flicked its tail at me. I think it lives in the big oak tree behind my building. 

But um... what were we talking about? Oh, right, the business stuff interfering. Yeah, so missing that utility payment was pretty bad, and I know I need to get back to my clients, but I just keep getting distracted by the art display and... everything else.

Um, yeah, the worry is... it's a lot, honestly. That's actually why I came in to see you, because ever since I tried to turn my art into a real freelance business, I just keep getting so wound up over the invoices and all those client messages. And then I avoid them until I'm literally just sitting there crying at my kitchen table, or forgetting normal stuff like paying a bill. 

My kitchen table is actually where I do most of my painting, too. It’s this gorgeous reclaimed wood farmhouse table I found on Facebook Marketplace. The guy who sold it to me was moving to Colorado to start an alpaca farm. Can you imagine? Alpacas are so funny-looking. They have those really big eyes and fluffy necks. I saw a video once of an alpaca getting sheared and it looked so ridiculously skinny underneath all that fluff. I think they use the fleece to make yarn, which makes sense because I knitted this scarf once out of alpaca yarn and it was the softest thing I've ever touched. I tried to knit a matching beanie for it, but I dropped a stitch somewhere in the middle and it ended up looking like a lopsided bowl. I ended up giving it to my neighbor's toddler to use as a sleeping bag for his stuffed animals. He has this massive collection of stuffed dinosaurs. The T-Rex is his favorite, but he can't pronounce it right, so he calls it a 'Tea-Rocks.' It's so cute. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Something about feeling guilty?

patient.answer:
Um, with friends and family? Not really, no. They don't really know much about the business side of things. My mom just thinks it's nice that I'm painting again. She always loved my paintings when I was little. She used to frame them and put them up all over the house, even the really bad ones where the people looked like stick figures with giant heads. 

Actually, I found one of those old paintings when I was helping her clean out her attic last weekend. The attic was so dusty, I was sneezing the whole time. I think I'm allergic to dust mites or something. I bought this special air purifier for my apartment because of it, and it has this little light that changes color depending on how clean the air is. It’s usually blue, but whenever I cook, it turns bright red. I’m not sure if that means I’m a bad cook or if my stove is just really smoky. I made stir-fry the other night and the smoke alarm went off, which was terrifying because my cat, Barnaby, completely freaked out and hid under the sofa for three hours. I had to lure him out with tuna water. He loves tuna water, but only from the cans that are packed in spring water, not the ones in oil. If I give him the oil kind, he just sniffs it and gives me this look of absolute betrayal. 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Oh, my family. Yeah, no, the business stuff hasn't really caused any problems with them. I just keep that part to myself.

patient.answer:
Um, no, I don't think it's that. I mean, I know my art is good, and people usually really like it when they see it. It's just the... the business part of it that freaks me out. The invoices and the formal emails. But the art itself, I'm really proud of. Like, I just finished this watercolor of a blue heron last week. I actually had to go to the art supply store downtown just to get a specific shade of cerulean blue for the water. 

I love that store so much, it always smells like cedar and linseed oil. But the parking there is just an absolute nightmare. I had to park three blocks away and right as I got out of my car, it started pouring rain. I didn't have an umbrella, so I had to use this empty canvas tote bag over my head to keep my hair dry. It was one of those canvas bags they give out for free at the farmer's market. I try to go to the farmer's market every Sunday to get these fresh sourdough loaves from this guy named Ted. Ted has this massive beard, like, it goes all the way down to his chest, and he told me he puts this special oil in it that smells like pine needles. 

I actually bought some pine-scented candles once because I thought it would make my apartment feel cozy, like a cabin in the woods, but they just made the whole place smell like a cheap car air freshener. You know those little cardboard green trees people hang from their rearview mirrors? My dad always had one of those in his truck when I was growing up. He drove this beat-up old Chevy that made a horrible rattling noise whenever he went over forty miles an hour. 

But um... wait, what did you ask me? Something about my clients not liking my work? Yeah, no, they like it fine. It's just... actually doing the business part and sending the emails that I can't seem to do.

Um, judged? No, I don't think so. I mean, my clients are usually really nice. It's not that I think they're going to yell at me or say I'm doing a bad job. It's just... I don't know, it's just the actual act of doing it that feels like too much. Looking at the numbers and figuring out the taxes and all that. Taxes are so confusing. I tried to use one of those online tax programs last year, and it kept asking me all these questions about deductions and depreciation, and I had no idea what any of it meant. 

I ended up calling my uncle Dave for help because he used to be an accountant, but he talks so slow. Like, painfully slow. And he always breathes really heavily into the phone, like he just ran up a flight of stairs. He lives in Florida now, in one of those retirement communities where everyone drives golf carts everywhere. He sent me a picture of his golf cart last Christmas, and he had put these little reindeer antlers on the roof and a red nose on the front bumper. It was kind of funny, but also a little weird. He said they have a golf cart parade every year, and last year someone decorated theirs like a giant flamingo. Flamingos are such strange birds. Why do they stand on one leg? I read once that it's to conserve body heat, but they live in warm places, so that doesn't really make sense, does it? 

But um... wait, what were you asking? Oh, about being criticized? Yeah, no, it's not that. It's just the business stuff itself that I can't handle.

Um, afraid of failing? I don't... I don't know if it's fear of failing, exactly. I mean, I know I'm a good artist. People buy my stuff. It's just... the thought of opening those emails and seeing all the requests and the deadlines, it just makes my chest feel all tight. Like when I try to drink coffee too fast in the morning. I've been trying to switch to tea, actually, because coffee makes me jittery. I got this loose-leaf chamomile blend from this little shop down the street. The woman who owns it is so nice, she always gives me free samples. Last time, she gave me this peppermint one that she said was good for digestion. 

I don't really have digestion problems, but I drank it anyway. It tasted kind of like toothpaste, to be honest. I used to use this organic toothpaste that tasted like fennel, which was awful. It was like brushing my teeth with black licorice. I hate black licorice. My grandma used to keep a bowl of it on her coffee table, the kind that looks like little black jellybeans. We'd always try to sneak the red ones when she wasn't looking, but she always knew. She had eyes in the back of her head, I swear. She could tell if we even touched the bowl. 

But um... wait, what were we talking about? Failing? Yeah, I don't think it's about failing. It's just... the business side is just so overwhelming, I can't even bring myself to look at it.

Um, relieved? I'm not sure... I haven't really thought about just stopping completely. I mean, if I wasn't doing my art, what would I even do? Just get a regular job again? I used to work at this bakery a few years ago, and I don't really want to go back to that. I always came home covered in flour. Like, a ridiculous amount of flour. It would get all in my hair and my shoes, and even all over my car seats. 

My car seats are black, so you could see every single white speck. I tried vacuuming it with one of those little hand-held vacuums, but it barely had any suction. I bought it off an infomercial late at night when I couldn't sleep. You know those commercials that come on at like 2 AM? The guy was yelling about how it could pick up bowling balls. Which is so stupid, why would anyone need to vacuum up a bowling ball? I don't even like bowling anyway. The shoes they make you wear are just so gross. You just know a thousand other people have sweat in them. My cousin rented a pair once and got a terrible case of athlete's foot, and he had to use this special cream that smelled exactly like sulfur. It made his whole house smell like rotten eggs for a week. 

But, um... wait, what did you ask me? If I'd feel relieved if I quit? Yeah, I don't know. I'm really not sure. I haven't really pictured not doing it.
